list.title: Reduced risk of severe illness, hospitalization, and death:
list.snippet: Vaccines significantly reduce the risk of developing severe COVID-19 infection, requiring hospitalization, or dying from the virus.

list.title: Protection against new variants:
list.snippet: While vaccine effectiveness may vary slightly against different variants, vaccines provide a level of protection against emerging strains.

list.title: Reduced transmission:
list.snippet: By preventing infection or reducing its severity, vaccines help limit the spread of the virus to others.

list.title: Long-lasting immunity:
list.snippet: Most vaccines provide durable immunity for several months to years.

list.title: Safety and efficacy:
list.snippet: COVID-19 vaccines have undergone rigorous testing and are generally considered safe and effective.

list.title: Mild side effects:
list.snippet: Most people experience mild side effects after vaccination, such as pain, redness, swelling, fatigue, or headache. These typically resolve within a few days.

list.title: Rare but serious adverse events:
list.snippet: Very rare but serious adverse events, such as allergic reactions or myocarditis (inflammation of the heart muscle), have been reported. However, these events are extremely uncommon.

list.title: Vaccine hesitancy:
list.snippet: Some people may be hesitant to get vaccinated due to concerns about safety, efficacy, or personal beliefs.

list.title: Need for boosters:
list.snippet: Depending on the vaccine type and the length of time since the initial vaccination, booster shots may be necessary to maintain optimal protection.

list.title: Limited effectiveness in immunocompromised individuals:
list.snippet: Vaccines may be less effective in people with weakened immune systems.
